title: The tracked tree passes publish's GUID scan, so a first publish is not refused
goal: Every GUID that kbpublic.file_hits reports over the tracked, non-private files (the _tools test and fixture files, kb/public CSV and XML data, and the item files that quote one) is classified: a patterned synthetic test id, an official published Microsoft id or an RFC example is allowlisted in _tools/tests_allowlist.txt with a reason line, and nothing else is allowlisted; a GUID that looks like a real tenant or object id is not allowlisted by an agent but listed for the operator. A test named publish_tree_guid_clean runs the scan over git ls-files (private paths and pinned artifacts left out as publish leaves them out) and fails on any unallowlisted GUID, so BG-svpvanw4's stricter scan lets a first publish pass. Found by mac-seventh: 24 tracked files would be refused.
